questions.explain: The chapter builds cost modeling on a dimensional cost attribution registry (CostAttribution.Ownership) plus a Query Store view estimating per-query compute cost at $0.048/vCPU-hour and I/O cost from logical reads — cost is treated as a runtime metric sampled like CPU.
options: Monthly invoice review meetings
A dimensional cost attribution registry mapping database objects to cost centers, plus Query Store-based per-query cost estimates
A single Excel spreadsheet
Vendor-provided cost dashboards only
questions.q: What is the foundation of cost modeling as a first-class metric in the chapter?

questions.explain: The Tier 1 query governance sets statement timeouts by cost center: data science exploratory workloads get 30-second limits on production replicas, while OLTP application roles get 5-second timeouts, enforced via Resource Governor or connection pool configuration.
options: All queries get unlimited runtime
Both get the same 60-second timeout
Data science gets 30-second queries on production replicas; OLTP roles get 5-second timeouts
Only the primary database is governed
questions.q: How does the Tier 1 statement timeout enforcement differ between data science and OLTP roles?

questions.explain: The forecast produces days_until_breach, and the graduated ladder tightens statement timeouts by 20% below 7 days, activates hard throttling below 3 days, and only logs a warning above 14 days — acting on the forecast, not the current spend.
options: Do nothing until the budget is exceeded
Act on the forecast: log above 14 days, tighten statement timeouts 20% below 7 days, hard-throttle below 3 days
Immediately shut down all non-production databases
Only send a monthly email report
questions.q: How does the predictive forecasting ladder use the days_until_breach forecast to protect monthly budgets?

questions.explain: The scoring function is Action_Score = W_cost*alpha - W_sla*beta - W_avail*gamma; the chapter gives examples like a startup using alpha=0.7, beta=0.2, gamma=0.1 versus financial services with alpha=0.3, beta=0.4, gamma=0.3.
options: Action_Score = W_cost*alpha - W_sla*beta - W_avail*gamma, with alpha/beta/gamma encoding organizational risk tolerance
Score = total savings minus nothing else
Score = SLA risk only
The highest-dollar action always executes autonomously
questions.q: What is the multi-dimensional cost tradeoff engine's composite scoring function?

questions.explain: On a 30-day feedback cycle: if savings predictions overestimate by more than 20%, the cost model coefficients ($/vCPU-hour, $/GB-IO) are recalibrated; if SLA breaches were predicted under 0.2 risk three or more times, beta increases by 0.05 per event up to a maximum of 0.6.
options: Actions are never re-evaluated after execution
Coefficients are fixed forever; only thresholds change
If savings predictions overestimate by >20% the unit cost coefficients are recalibrated; repeated SLA underestimation raises the beta weight
Calibration is performed manually once a year
questions.q: How does the 30-day calibration loop adjust the cost model and scoring weights?
